entry.title: Thomas's cage monophonic position conjecture
entry.statement:
Let a $(d,g)$-cage $G$ be a graph of degree $d$ and girth $g$, and let $\operatorname{mp}(G)$ denote its monophonic position number. **Thomas's conjecture.** For sufficiently large $g$, the monophonic position number of a $(d,g)$-cage $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{mp}(G)<d.
$$

The survey presents this as a computationally suggested conjecture, and no resolution is given.

Later alias search found the same question at 349120 in expanded-corpus-r41/results.json; inherited outcome hold_literal_only retained and route stopped.

entry.title: Prowse–Woodall $(a:b)$-choosability equivalence conjecture
entry.literal_statement: Let $L$ be an $a$-list assignment on a graph $G$. The graph is **$(a:b)$-choosable** when every such assignment admits a choice of a $b$-element sublist at each vertex whose selected lists are disjoint across edges. Let $(G)_b$ denote the graph operation used in the source. **Prowse–Woodall's $(a:b)$-choosability equivalence conjecture.** For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, a graph $G$ is $(a:b)$-choosable if and only if $(G)_b$ is $a$-choosable. The supplied text says this conjecture was disproved by Dvořák et al. using a 4-choosable graph that is not $(8:2)$-choosable.

entry.title: The pivot containment conjecture
entry.ordinary_result_or_gap: Conjecture 11.13 concerns every singular-space pivot, not merely the pivots constructed from irreducible configurations. Theorem 5.6 supplies only the latter subset. See ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md for triangular elimination and steady-recursion gaps.
entry.literal_statement:
Let $W_{2n}$ be the set of words of length $2n$. For a word $w$, let $H(w)$ be its singular-vector space, let $\mathrm{Pvt}(w)$ be the set of pivot sign sequences of a basis of $H(w)$, let $\mathrm{SConf}(w)$ be the set of steady arc configurations, and define $\mu_w$ by

$$
(\mu_w(C))_i=+
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i\in\operatorname{LC}(C).
$$

**The pivot containment conjecture.** For every $w\in W_{2n}$,

$$
\mathrm{Pvt}(w)\subset\mu_w(\mathrm{SConf}(w)).
$$

The paper explains that irreducible configurations already give the opposite containment into the pivot set, so this conjecture would imply the stated combinatorial consequence. No resolution is given.

entry.title: The irreducible-to-steady arc-configuration conjecture
entry.ordinary_result_or_gap: Conjecture 11.14 asks for a steady configuration with the identical left-end set. Cardinality inequalities and uniqueness on each separate class do not supply the inclusion. See sustained left-end recursion attempt.
entry.literal_statement:
Let $W_{2n}$ be the set of words of length $2n$, let $\mathrm{IConf}(w)$ and $\mathrm{SConf}(w)$ be the irreducible and steady arc configurations of $w$, and let $\mu_w$ record the set of left ends of an arc configuration. **The irreducible-to-steady arc-configuration conjecture.** For every $w\in W_{2n}$,

$$
\mu_w(\mathrm{IConf}(w))\subset\mu_w(\mathrm{SConf}(w)).
$$

Equivalently, every set of left ends arising from an irreducible arc configuration also arises from a steady arc configuration. This is presented as a purely combinatorial consequence of the pivot conjecture; no resolution is stated.

entry.title: Gravier–Maffray list-coloring conjecture for claw-free graphs
entry.statement:
A graph is **claw-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,3}$. Let $\chi(G)$ and $\chi_\ell(G)$ denote the chromatic and list chromatic numbers. **Gravier–Maffray's conjecture.** For every claw-free graph $G$,

$$
\chi_\ell(G)=\chi(G).
$$

This is the broad chromatic-choosability conjecture for claw-free graphs; the supplied text does not resolve it in general.

entry.title: Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture for independent position chromatic numbers
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $\overline{G}$ be its complement, and choose $\pi\in\{\operatorname{gp},\operatorname{mp}\}$, where $\operatorname{gp}$ and $\operatorname{mp}$ denote general and monophonic position, respectively. Let $\chi_{\pi_{\rm i}}(G)$ denote the chromatic number whose color classes are independent $\pi$-position sets. **Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{\pi_{\rm i}}(G)+\chi_{\pi_{\rm i}}(\overline{G})\leq n+1.
$$

The survey identifies this as an open problem; no general proof or counterexample is reported.

entry.title: Fitzpatrick's fractional general position conjecture for square grids
entry.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, let $P_n\mathbin{\square}P_n$ be the $n\times n$ Cartesian grid, and let $\operatorname{gp}_f$ denote the fractional general position number. For even $n\geq 3$, define the lower bound from Theorem 2.1 by

$$
\frac{n^2-2t(t+1)}{n-t-\frac12}
$$

for $0\leq t\leq n/2$. For odd $n\geq 3$, use the two lower bounds from Theorem 2.2, namely

$$
\frac{n^2+1-8k^2}{n-2k}
$$

and

$$
\frac{n^2-1-8(k^2+k)}{n-2k-1}
$$

with the parameter ranges specified there. **Fitzpatrick's conjecture.** The lower bound from Theorem 2.1 is optimal for even $n$, and the bound from Theorem 2.2 is optimal for odd $n$.

Exact values were known in the survey only for small orders, although the lower bound had been shown best possible through $n=10$; the conjectured optimality for all even and odd orders remains open.

entry.title: Kruft's lower general position number conjecture for Cartesian products
entry.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $G\mathbin{\square}H$ denote their Cartesian product, and let $\operatorname{gp}^-(G)$ denote the lower general position number of $G$. **Kruft's conjecture.** For any graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
\operatorname{gp}^-(G\mathbin{\square}H)\geq\min\{\operatorname{gp}^-(G),\operatorname{gp}^-(H)\}.
$$

The inequality has been verified for all pairs of graphs of order at most six, but remains open in general.
